extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, STIC (Scientific and Technical Information Center) staff, and other patent search/classification personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and quality standards for USPTO examiners in obtaining, searching, translating, and classifying prior art (foreign patents, non‑patent literature, and classification data) using STIC, Global Dossier, and classification manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: INID bibliographic data elements — priority application identifiers (31-33)
rubrics_metrics.description: (31) Serial number assigned to the priority application; (32) Date of filing of the priority application; (33) Two-letter code, according to WIPO Standard ST.3, identifying the authority with which the priority application was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When data coded (31), (32), and (33) are presented together, category code (30) can be used. For Hague Agreement international deposits use two-letter code “WO.”

rubrics_metrics.name: INID dates of availability/publication (40-46)
rubrics_metrics.description: (40) Date(s) of making information available to the public; (43) Date of publication of the industrial design before examination by printing or similar process, or making it available to the public by any other means; (44) Date of publication after examination, but before registration; (45) Date of publication of the registered industrial design; (46) Date of expiration of deferment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat publication/availability dates as bibliographic data elements to document public disclosure timelines relevant to novelty and priority determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: INID miscellaneous information for design documents (50-58)
rubrics_metrics.description: (50) Miscellaneous Information; (51) International Classification for Industrial Designs (Locarno class/subclass); (52) National classification; (53) Identification of design(s) affected in multiple filings; (54) Designation of article(s) or product(s) covered or title of the design; (55) Reproduction of the industrial design (drawing/photograph) and explanations; (56) List of prior art documents if separate from descriptive text; (57) Description of characteristic features including colors; (58) Date of recording of amendments (changes in name/address, ownership, renunciation, international deposit termination of protection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code (52) should be preceded by the two-letter country code (WIPO ST.3) in parentheses. Item (55) is a minimum data element for design documents only.

rubrics_metrics.name: INID references and related application identifiers (60-66)
rubrics_metrics.description: (60) References to application(s) and registration(s); (62) Serial number(s) and, if available, filing date(s) of related applications/registrations/documents (including divisionals); (66) Serial number(s) of application/registration of designs which are variant(s) of the present one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category code (60) should be used by countries which were previously part of another entity to identify bibliographic data elements relating to applications/registrations announced by the former entity's office.

rubrics_metrics.name: INID identification of parties and owners (70-89)
rubrics_metrics.description: (70) Identification of parties concerned with the application/registration; (71) Name(s) and address(es) of applicant(s); (72) Name(s) of the creator(s) if known; (73) Name(s) and address(es) of owner(s); (74) Name(s)/address(es) of representative(s); (78) Name(s)/address(es) of new owner(s) after ownership change; (80-89) Data related to international deposits (Hague Agreement), designated Contracting Parties, statements in international application, review/appeal indications, designated contracting states under regional conventions, and owner information (habitual residence, nationality, domicile, state of real/commercial establishment, “Applicant’s Contracting Party”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration occurred on or before making the design available to the public, indicating the owner(s) meets minimum data requirement; otherwise indicating applicant(s) does. INID codes (81)–(88) should use two-letter WIPO ST.3 country codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining foreign patent copies — sources and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign patents are available to examiners via USPTO automated search tools (PE2E SEARCH, Foreign Patent Finder, Global Dossier), other foreign patent websites, Derwent World Patents Index, and the Foreign Patents Service Center (FPSC) in STIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may request copies from STIC or FPSC, submit online Foreign Patent Request Forms via STIC intranet, retrieve documents themselves via PE2E SEARCH/FIT, or use Global Dossier Public Access for PCT/WIPO-CASE participating offices. Older documents may require retrieval from microfilm or print in Main STIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when unprinted or unavailable foreign patent documents surface
rubrics_metrics.description: If non‑printed patent documents or documents not in search files come to an examiner's attention (e.g., cited in motions or applicant submissions), STIC will obtain a copy from its collection or the origin country's patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For unprinted documents STIC will request that the country indicate date of granting and date the specification was made available to the public on provided copies. Examiners can request equivalents via Global Dossier or request assistance from STIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FIT (Foreign Image and Text) database
rubrics_metrics.description: PE2E SEARCH includes FIT, a collection of foreign documents in full English text (abstract, description, claims) with images; documents are either natively English or vendor-translated using human and machine sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIT offers full-text English documents to facilitate examiner searching and citation; examiners should prefer automated systems for current patent documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation resources and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may consult translators in STIC’s Translations Service Center for oral assistance and may request human (written) translations of pertinent portions or full translation of foreign references at any point in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are encouraged to use machine translations, oral assistance, and language reference resources, but may request human translations via STIC Translation Request Form. The Translations Service Center checks for existing equivalents/translations before processing requests; written translations are delivered by email and are indexed in a translations database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non‑patent literature (NPL) as references
rubrics_metrics.description: All printed publications may be used as references; the date to be cited is the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STIC maintains EICs and collections to assist examiners in locating NPL. NPL resources help determine anticipation (35 U.S.C. 102) and obviousness (35 U.S.C. 103). See MPEP § 2128 for citation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC collections — books and purchase requests
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC selects and purchases primarily English-language publications (priority to electronic resources) based on examiner and expert recommendations. A legacy print collection exists in Main STIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners can request purchases via NPL Purchase Request Form; all STIC resources are discoverable through STIC Online Catalog. E-books may be purchased if print not available; Interlibrary Loan used when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC periodicals collection
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC provides access to many electronic periodicals and a legacy collection of print periodicals, including titles pertinent to design patent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for new subscriptions accepted year-round; all periodicals discoverable via STIC Online Catalog.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC foreign patent documents collection and access
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO receives foreign patent documents via exchange agreements; STIC's collection is the most comprehensive in the U.S., with current items accessible via automated search tools and historical documents on paper or remote sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official foreign patent journals are shelved by country; some journals include abstracts. Examiners may use automated tools to look up, view, and print documents; STIC staff assist in retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC special collections and digitization
rubrics_metrics.description: Rare and historical book collections have been digitized to provide electronic access and preservation; majority of collections are now electronic books, journals, and foreign patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections are arranged by Technology Center and accessible via STIC Online Catalog; examiners should check TC-specific collections and ask EIC staff for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to locate materials in STIC — STIC Online Catalog usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The STIC Online Catalog is the primary tool for locating electronic books/journals, databases, subscription resources, print books, and other materials; electronic catalog records contain direct links to resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access via Patent Examiner’s Toolkit or STIC NPL website. Most electronic resources are accessible from the USPTO network; some commercial databases require account creation and supervisor approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan policy for STIC materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All STIC print materials may be checked out except non-circulating items (reference publications, print journals, foreign patent documents, microfilm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may request materials from other libraries; for official business, Reference Delivery Branch can provide table of contents or photocopies. STIC staff can advise on lending practices of other libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC reference services
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC staff provide assistance on finding information, using STIC resources, and updates on service requests via in-person, phone, email, instant message, or Ask‑STIC chat-room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If encountering problems locating materials or answers, examiners should consult STIC staff for guidance and assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art and bibliographic search services (STIC EICs)
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC EIC staff perform prior art and bibliographic searches using commercial databases (ProQuest Dialog, STN, Questel‑Orbit, IP.com, etc.) and can provide searches that include abstracts, chemical structures, DNA sequences, and full text PDFs where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may submit Text/Regular Form for prior art/text searches or Litigation Form for bibliographic/legal searches. Completed searches are emailed to examiners. STIC staff can perform sequence searches for specific TCs and provide introductory training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners conducting their own searches — training and vendor accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may perform searches independently if they obtain approval for commercial database logins and receive vendor training via USPTO Learning Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual assistance in searching databases is available from EIC staff, especially for complex chemical or sequence searches. Examiners must obtain SPE approval for database access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Patents Service Center services
rubrics_metrics.description: FPSC staff perform patent family searches, identify English-language equivalents, determine priority/publication dates, perform inventor or abstract number searches, retrieve bibliographic documents, and provide foreign classification information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FPSC can supplement online searches with manual searches of foreign journals, concordances, and indexes, and provide training on using foreign patent collections. Public may order copies from FPSC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlibrary loans and borrowed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: STIC will obtain materials (journal articles, book chapters) not available in-house through Interlibrary Loan for official business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests submitted to STIC EIC facility or via electronic form on STIC NPL website. STIC has purchasing agreements with libraries across the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site photocopying of STIC materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Photocopy machines are available for examiners to copy STIC materials which do not circulate or materials they prefer not to check out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use machines for non-circulating materials or when checkout is undesirable; STIC policy governs photocopying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining publication dates for foreign and U.S. publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for earliest date of publication or first distribution should be made to STIC EIC facility; for U.S. publications, STIC staff can obtain day and month claimed by copyright owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreign publications STIC staff will obtain date information via correspondence; allow additional time for foreign queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tours and orientation of STIC services
rubrics_metrics.description: Special tours of STIC and its service centers can be arranged for examiners or outside groups by contacting the STIC EIC facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tours aid familiarity with STIC resources and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alien Property Custodian (A.P.C.) publications — citation and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications vested in the Alien Property Custodian during WWII were published in 1943 as A.P.C. published applications and must not be referred to as patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A.P.C. publications may be used as printed publications effective from their stated publication date for rejections. Cite them as: 'A.P.C. Application of ..., Ser. No. ..., Published ...'. The Patent Search Room contains bound volumes of A.P.C. published applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts, Abbreviatures, and Defensive Publications — handling and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts and Abbreviatures are USPTO publications of abandoned applications; Defensive Publications are USPTO publications of provisionally abandoned applications. Statutory Invention Registrations replaced Defensive Publications but relevant provisions were repealed for new filings after certain dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defensive Publications and Statutory Invention Registrations are included in subclass lists and subscription orders. Distinct numbering systems apply depending on publication date ranges; conversion tables exist for older numbering schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family information — sources and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent family information is available via commercial databases and USPTO automated tools; examiners may use Derwent World Patents Index (WPI), INPADOC, Common Citation Document website, Global Dossier, and other tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WPI is used for abstracts, inventor-name searches, IPC searches, publication dates and patent families; INPADOC is used for quick publication date/family checks (access in Austria has special rate arrangements). Global Dossier and Common Citation Document provide file histories and Office Actions for related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to foreign patent information and recommended databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may search WPI in-house, INPADOC, or request foreign patent searches through STIC; automated tools and FPSC services are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose database according to need: WPI for abstracts and comprehensive searches, INPADOC for quick family/publication date checks. STIC services can perform searches when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual of Classification (USPC) — role and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO maintains an electronic Manual of Classification for the U.S. Patent Classification System (USPC); classes have titles, numbers, and subclasses with definitions and notes. The Manual contains overviews, class lists by subject matter, by art unit, numeric arrangements, alphabetical arrangements, and class schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPC is static for utility classes (no longer updated after Dec 31, 2014) but remains active for design and plant classes. Use the Manual as a key to class/subclass definitions and notes rather than relying solely on brief titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index to the U.S. Patent Classification System (USPC) — usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Index is an alphabetical listing of technical/common terms referring to specific classes and subclasses and is used as an initial entry into the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not consider the Index exhaustive; scan appropriate class schedules and review definitions/notes of pertinent classifications even when the Index citation appears specific. Suggestions for Index changes are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class and subclass definitions in USPC — necessity of review
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPC classes have definitions that state subject matter in more detail than class/subclass titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study definitions to determine proper classification. Definitions and notes may change due to classification orders; examiners should periodically update personal definition sets and consult Classification Home Page for updates and Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition notes in USPC — two types and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition notes either (A) supplement definitions by explaining terms or giving examples, or (B) refer to related disclosures in other classes/subclasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review definition notes to understand scope and related areas for accurate classification and document placement.
